metadata.question: Did New York experience an air temperature difference of at least 24 degrees Celcius between January 29 and February 5, 2019?

data.raw_code: The user is asking about air temperature difference in New York between two specific dates in 2019. I need to: 1. Use a temperature dataset - ERA5 (ECMWF reanalysis) would be good for this as it provides reliable temperature data 2. Define New York geometry (I'll use a point for NYC) 3. Get temperature data for January 29, 2019 and February 5, 2019 4. Calculate the difference and check if it's >= 24°C 5. Handle cases where data might be missing Strategy: - Use ECMWF/ERA5/DAILY collection which has daily temperature data - Extract mean 2m air temperature for both dates - Convert from Kelvin to Celsius - Calculate absolute difference - Check if difference >= 24°C Potential issues: - Collection might be empty (C1) - Temperature values might be invalid (C3) - Need to validate temperature ranges (reasonable values for NYC in winter) ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions const nyc = ee.Geometry.Point([-74.0060, 40.7128]); // New York City // 2. Data Acquisition const era5 = ee.ImageCollection('ECMWF/ERA5/DAILY'); const jan29 = era5 .filterDate('2019-01-29', '2019-01-30') .select('mean_2m_air_temperature'); const feb5 = era5 .filterDate('2019-02-05', '2019-02-06') .select('mean_2m_air_temperature'); // Check if collections are empty const jan29Count = jan29.size().getInfo(); const feb5Count = feb5.size().getInfo(); console.log(`Jan29 Images: ${jan29Count}, Feb5 Images: ${feb5Count}`); if (jan29Count === 0 || feb5Count === 0) { console.log("C1"); return; } // Get first image from each collection const jan29Img = jan29.first(); const feb5Img = feb5.first(); // 3. Extract temperature values and convert from Kelvin to Celsius const jan29Temp = jan29Img .reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: nyc, scale: 10000, maxPixels: 1e9 }) .get('mean_2m_air_temperature') .getInfo(); const feb5Temp = feb5Img .reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: nyc, scale: 10000, maxPixels: 1e9 }) .get('mean_2m_air_temperature') .getInfo(); // Convert from Kelvin to Celsius const jan29TempC = jan29Temp - 273.15; const feb5TempC = feb5Temp - 273.15; const tempDiff = Math.abs(jan29TempC - feb5TempC); console.log(`Jan29 Temp: ${jan29TempC.toFixed(1)}°C`); console.log(`Feb5 Temp: ${feb5TempC.toFixed(1)}°C`); console.log(`Difference: ${tempDiff.toFixed(1)}°C`); // 4. Validation & Final Answer // Check for invalid temperature values (NYC winter range: reasonable -20°C to +20°C) if (jan29TempC < -50 || jan29TempC > 50 || feb5TempC < -50 || feb5TempC > 50) { console.log("C3"); } else if (tempDiff >= 24) { console.log("A"); } else { console.log("B"); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
